definition: Penitent means remorseful about a wrong and moved to confess or make amends.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word penitent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know penitent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The penitent shoplifter returned to the store every Saturday for a year, working off what she had taken shelf by shelf.
Embarrassed is far milder than penitent — an awkward flush at being caught, with no real sorrow in it.
Remorseful is weaker than penitent — remorse feels the sorrow, while a penitent person carries it forward into confession and amends.

Regretful is the mildest of the sorry words: you wish it had gone otherwise, and there it ends — no confession required, sometimes no fault at all. Penitent is regret with weight and direction: sorrow over a real wrong that moves toward confession and repair.

Repentant stresses the turn: the wrongdoer renounces what they did and changes course, the word of sermons and courtrooms. Penitent walks beside it but leans toward the debt still owed — confession made, amends paid, sorrow turned into long repair rather than a single turning point.

The mural on the community center wall took the volunteers a full summer to paint.
The night it was defaced, most people expected the usual outcome: a shrug, a denial, maybe a fine nobody would pay.
Instead, a sixteen-year-old showed up at the center's front desk the next morning and admitted the tagging before anyone had named a suspect.
He was, by every account, genuinely penitent — not just sorry he had been reckless, but set on repairing it.
He asked for the paint bill, worked it off in weekend shifts, and spent October repainting the ruined corner under the muralist's direction.
When the wall was rededicated, the muralist said the apology she trusted was the one that had shown up with a brush in its hand.
